assertion.rationale: F1: data-api had ingressExternal:true and zero inbound authentication (app.ts:56) — anyone who found the FQDN could read Defender posture, Dependabot alerts and Log Analytics results, and loop full table scans. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so the app is reachable only from inside the Container Apps environment. Both frontends already proxied /api/ server-side before this change — control-tower's and launch-ops' nginx.conf.template both carry a `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; ... }` rule, verified present in both rather than assumed — so no legitimate caller lost access; DATA_API_ORIGIN still resolves the app's FQDN, which Azure Container Apps assigns to internal-ingress apps too. The /healthz convenience the app's header comment previously cited is now reached with `az containerapp exec` instead of a browser. F2: the MCP auth gate was inert in the shipped configuration — it threw only in backendMode 'cloud', MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is set nowhere in infra/ or .github/, so /healthz reported auth.enforced:false to anyone. F2 is now CLOSED (Tasks 4 and 5). Task 4 closed the application half: loadInboundAuth (auth-gate.ts) no longer conditions enforcement on backendMode, so local mode — the configuration that actually ships — now fails closed at boot without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN or an explicit MCP_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED opt-out, and the gate is mounted ahead of the body parser. Task 5 closed the infra half: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep no longer declares a `@secure()` mcpAuthToken parameter (deleted, along with demo.bicepparam's empty default); the mcp-tools container app instead resolves the mcp-auth-token secret directly from the platform Key Vault at runtime via a keyVaultUrl + identity reference, using a Key Vault Secrets User grant on the mcp-tools UAMI (module mcpKvGrant, reusing modules/key-vault-secrets-user-role.bicep, previously unreferenced since the 2026-08-24 Anthropic removal). The token therefore never enters this template, demo.bicepparam, ARM deployment history or a what-if log, and no workflow reads or exports it. MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is now set explicitly via the mcpToolsBackendMode parameter (default 'local') instead of being absent from every workflow. F3: the Direct Line token endpoint minted tokens to unauthenticated callers whenever DIRECTLINE_ALLOWED_ORIGINS was unset or Origin was absent, and that path carries the MCP token, which made F2's gate irrelevant to it. F3 is now CLOSED (Task 7): directline-token.mjs now refuses with 500 when the allow-list is unset (so an unbound token is never minted) and with 403 when Origin is absent or not allow-listed, checked as two separate conditions rather than one combined boolean so neither can skip the other. F13: zero workload RBAC is expressed anywhere in IaC — the only role assignments in the estate are deployer-to-Owner and verifier-to-Reader, both at subscription scope in PowerShell; seven documented workload grants (data-api, mcp-tools, cost-ingest) exist nowhere as code, so access is not limited to authorized users, processes or devices by construction. Task 12 expresses five of the seven in code: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now grants data-api and mcp-tools Log Analytics Reader (scoped to the platform LAW, modules/log-analytics-reader-role.bicep) and Security Reader (subscription scope, modules/workload-role-assignments.bicep), mcp-tools additionally gets Cost Management Reader (same module), data-api's SQL contained-database user is expressed in data/seed/sql/900-contained-users.sql, and data-api's Fabric workspace Viewer grant is expressed via a new Add-FabricWorkspaceRoleAssignment function in infra/fabric/fabric-api.psm1 wired through provision-workspace.ps1's -DataApiPrincipalId parameter. Two of the seven remain unexpressed and F13 stays OPEN because of them: Cost Management service -> Storage Blob Data Contributor is owned by Task 17 (F15), since the export's identity is created by the layer-06-platform.yml workflow, not Bicep; cost-ingest -> Storage Blob Data Reader is blocked on F19 (cost-ingest has no Function App, and therefore no identity, anywhere in this repo's IaC, despite infra-up.yml:31 claiming otherwise). Building Task 12 also surfaced F20 (the SQL grant above is expressed but nothing re-runs the seed script after L7 creates the identity, so it does not yet apply in a single infra-up.yml pass) and F21 (mls-verifier's own documented Fabric workspace Viewer grant does not exist either, breaking the L5 Verifier audit — a different principal, tracked separately). Overall status stays GAP: F1, F2 and F3 are all now closed, but F13 remains open — five of seven grants landed, two did not — and is this control's only remaining contributor.

recommendation: Close the two remaining grants: Task 17 (F15) must add the Cost Management service's Storage Blob Data Contributor grant when it gives the cost export an identity; F19 must be fixed (cost-ingest provisioned as a real Function App with its own identity) before its Storage Blob Data Reader grant can be expressed at all. Add a criterion asserting each principal holds exactly its expected roles once both land. (Setting ingressExternal:false on data-api, the MCP auth gate default and Key Vault token resolution, the Direct Line origin guard fail-closed fix, and five of F13's seven workload RBAC grants recommended here previously, are all DONE — Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7 and 12.)
